name: Loop_CombinePolygons
formula: =LAMBDA(verticesText,verticesArrText,[count],LET(i, IF(ISOMITTED(count), 1, count), n, ROWS(verticesArrText), verticesA, VALUE({ref}TextToArray(verticesText)), verticesB, VALUE({ref}TextToArray(INDEX(verticesArrText, i, 1))), combinedPolys, {ref}CombineTwoPolygons(verticesA, verticesB), isCombined, ROWS(combinedPolys) = 1, returnVerticesArrText, IF(isCombined, IF(n = 1, combinedPolys, VSTACK(combinedPolys, {ref}RemoveRow(verticesArrText, i))), VSTACK(verticesArrText, verticesText)), out, IF(OR(i = n, isCombined), returnVerticesArrText, {ref}Loop_CombinePolygons(verticesText, verticesArrText, i + 1)), out))
comment: Tries to union one polygon with each polygon in a column. verticesText is one strict ARRAYTOTEXT of (x, y) rows. verticesArrText is a column of the same kind of string. count is optional and is the 1-based row to try; omit it to start at 1. A union replaces that row with the combined polygon. No union appends verticesText. A string shorter than 2 characters returns #VALUE!. Last Update at 2026-11-03.
